changes.before: From the chapter on courage: death for a cause unworthy of dying for, was called a dog's death. He quotes the Prince of Mito: to rush into the thick of battle and to be slain in it is easy enough, and the merest churl is equal to the task; but it is true courage to live when it is right to live, and to die only when it is right to die. And he distinguishes explicitly: to run all kinds of hazards, to place oneself in jeopardy, to rush into the jaws of death, are often identified with valour, and in the profession of arms such rashness — what Shakespeare calls valour misbegotten — is unjustly applauded; but not so in the Precepts of Knighthood.
changes.after: From the chapter on courage: death for a cause unworthy of dying for, was called a dog's death. He quotes Mitsukuni, the Prince of Mito: to rush into the thick of battle and to be slain in it is easy enough, and the merest churl is equal to the task; but it is true courage to live when it is right to live, and to die only when it is right to die. And he distinguishes explicitly: to run all kinds of hazards, to place oneself in jeopardy, to rush into the jaws of death, are often identified with valour, and in the profession of arms such rashness — what Shakespeare calls valour misbegotten — is unjustly applauded; but not so in the Precepts of Knighthood.

semantic_notes: All 57 units, title/deck and complete comparison table independently read. Nitobe's contrary direction to Hagakure remains limited to one opening passage and one issue, not a systematic revision of an entire tradition.
Responsibility never becomes ownership or another person's power of disposal. Criticism remains principally ground conflict, not an invented contradiction in Nitobe's system.
Argumentative insufficiency of willing and the Abraham counterexample remain distinct from internal inconsistency. Consent is not treated as authorising merely instrumental use.

The preservation/acquiescence boundary is subject standing after concession, not cost magnitude. The shame, willingness and evidentiary-limit questions remain unresolved. Source u37 formulation is retained without manufacturing an opposite-applications interpretation.
